US Treasury Ends Ownership Reporting Rules

The US Treasury has ended ownership reporting rules for US companies. This decision eliminates reporting requirements for US companies and persons under the Corporate Transparency Act. The Act remains in place, but the reporting rules are no longer applicable. The US State Department has also released a report on fiscal transparency, finding that 73 of 139 governments meet the requirements. The report highlights the importance of transparency in government finances. The Treasury's decision affects US businesses, which are no longer required to report ownership information.
